passage: On Monday morning in Pema's Gangtok school, Varun ran up to her and said, “Everyone says you told Sir about my lost pen!” Pema felt her cheeks flush. She hadn't. Her first instinct was to shout, “Who said that?” But she took a breath. “Who told you? Let's ask Sir together.” Varun blinked. They walked to Sir, who said the pen was found in the library. Varun said, “Sorry, I believed the rumour.” Pema nodded, her heart still fast. “I was angry, but I'm glad we checked.” They walked back to class, and Varun handed her a biscuit. 🙂

qa.q: Where was the pen found?
qa.a: In the library.

qa.q: Why did Pema take a breath and not shout at once, and what was she feeling?
qa.a: She felt angry and wanted to shout at whoever started the rumour, but wanted the truth more, so she took a breath and offered to ask Sir together.

qa.q: Why did checking with Sir work better than hitting back with anger?
qa.a: It gave both of them facts, ended the rumour and did not add another hurt.

qa.q: How might Varun have felt on learning the truth?
qa.a: Varun probably felt embarrassed and sorry for believing the rumour, which is why Varun apologised and shared a biscuit.

grounding: A schoolchild faced with a rumour pauses, asks for facts and checks with an adult, rather than believing or hitting back.

passage: “They said you took my eraser!” Farida burst out at the door. Deepika froze. “What? Who said that?” “Everyone.” Deepika's mother, stirring dal, looked up. “Deepika, breathe. Farida, who exactly said it?” Farida hesitated. “Well... Rina said Tara said.” “So nobody saw it?” Farida shook her head. Deepika's chest was tight. “I didn't take it, but I understand why you're upset. Let's look in your bag together.” They found the eraser under a book. Farida's ears went red. “Sorry.” Deepika said, “Next time ask me first.” Her mother smiled and went back to the stove.

qa.q: Where did the girls find the eraser?
qa.a: Under a book in Farida's bag.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling when she heard the accusation, and what did she do with the feeling?
qa.a: She felt scared and upset, since her chest was tight, but she stayed calm and offered to look together.

qa.q: Why did Deepika's mother ask who exactly said it?
qa.a: She wanted facts before anyone believed the claim, and the answer showed that nobody had actually seen anything.

qa.q: How might Farida have felt when the eraser was found?
qa.a: She probably felt embarrassed and sorry, since her ears went red and she apologised.

grounding: A schoolchild faced with an accusation pauses, asks for facts and checks with the person involved.

passage: I'm Amandeep. Last term, a girl in our class told me, “Rukmini said your drawing was copied from the internet.” My face burned. Rukmini was my best friend. I wanted to march over and tell everyone that she copied her homework. Instead I made myself wait until lunch. I asked the girl, “Did you hear Rukmini say it?” She shrugged. “Someone told me.” So I went to Rukmini and asked straight: “Did you say my drawing was copied?” Rukmini looked shocked. “No! I said it looked so good it could be in a book!” Somewhere along the way, it had changed. If I'd hit back first, I'd have lost my best friend over a compliment.

qa.q: What had Rukmini actually said about the drawing?
qa.a: Rukmini said it looked so good it could be in a book.

qa.q: What was Amandeep feeling on hearing the rumour?
qa.a: Amandeep felt hurt and angry, face burning, and wanted to hit back at a best friend.

qa.q: What steps did Amandeep take before believing the rumour?
qa.a: Amandeep waited, asked the girl whether she heard it directly, and then checked with Rukmini.

qa.q: How did Rukmini react when asked?
qa.a: Rukmini was shocked, since she had actually given a compliment that got twisted along the way.

grounding: Shows a child pausing on hearing gossip, asking for facts and checking with the person involved instead of hitting back.

passage: Class note, Thursday. Simran, Class 5. This morning Dev's new pencil box went missing, and within ten minutes half the class was saying Chinmay took it. Someone had seen him “near the bag”. Chinmay went pale and started shouting that they were liars, and two boys shouted back. I stopped everything. “No one decides anything yet. What do we actually know?” We knew three things: the box was missing, Chinmay sits next to Dev, and nobody saw him take it. I asked the office helper to check lost property. The box was there; Dev had left it in the music room. I asked the class to say sorry to Chinmay, and they did. Tomorrow I'll talk to them about rumours.

qa.q: Where had Dev left the pencil box?
qa.a: Dev had left it in the music room.

qa.q: What was Chinmay feeling when he started shouting?
qa.a: Chinmay felt frightened and angry at being accused without proof.

qa.q: How did Simran stop the rumour from escalating?
qa.a: She stopped the shouting, asked the class what they actually knew and checked lost property before anyone decided.

qa.q: How did the class first treat the rumour?
qa.a: Half the class believed it quickly, just because Chinmay sat near Dev's bag.

grounding: Shows a child facing an accusation, and an adult pausing to ask for facts and check before anyone believes it.

passage: Wednesday. Farhan's diary. Today the whole bus was buzzing: “Pankaj got expelled! For fighting!” He hasn't come to school since Monday. Some boys were already making up what the fight was about. I felt sick. Pankaj is my friend, and he doesn't fight. I almost believed it anyway, because everyone was so sure. Then I thought: who actually knows? Not the boys on the bus. So at break I asked our class teacher, straight out. She said, “Pankaj has chickenpox. He'll be back next week. Please don't spread stories.” I told the boys on the way home. One of them said, “Oh.” I'm going to phone Pankaj tonight.

qa.q: Why was Pankaj really absent?
qa.a: Pankaj had chickenpox.

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling when the bus was buzzing with the rumour?
qa.a: Farhan felt sick and worried, and almost believed the rumour because everyone seemed so sure.

qa.q: How did Farhan check the rumour?
qa.a: Farhan thought about who actually knew and asked the class teacher directly, then told the boys the truth.

qa.q: How did the boys on the bus treat the rumour?
qa.a: They believed it and even made up details about the fight, spreading a story that wasn't true.

grounding: Shows a child hearing a rumour, pausing and checking the facts with an adult instead of believing it quickly.

passage: At the handpump behind the school, Deepu splashed his face and leaned close. "Nirmala told Sir you copied your maths from me. That's why he kept your notebook." Rafiq's fists tightened around his tiffin. He could already picture shouting at her in front of the whole class. Instead he stood still, counting the drips from the spout. "Did you hear her say it?" he asked. Deepu shrugged. "Someone told me." After lunch, Rafiq walked over to Nirmala, who was drawing a kolam pattern on her slate. "Did you tell Sir I copied?" Nirmala looked up, surprised. "No! Sir asked me to collect the notebooks with missing pages. Yours had one." Rafiq's fists opened. That afternoon Sir handed back his notebook with a note: finish page twelve.

qa.q: Where was Rafiq when Deepu told him the rumour?
qa.a: He was at the handpump behind the school.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling when his fists tightened around his tiffin?
qa.a: He felt angry and hurt, believing Nirmala had got him into trouble, and probably embarrassed that Sir had kept his notebook.

qa.q: What small step stopped the rumour from turning into a fight?
qa.a: Rafiq paused, asked Deepu whether he had heard it himself, and then checked directly with Nirmala instead of shouting at her.

qa.q: What would change if Rafiq had shouted at Nirmala in front of the class?
qa.a: Nirmala, who had only collected notebooks, would have been hurt and shamed for something untrue, and a quarrel could have grown out of gossip.

grounding: It illustrates a school-age child meeting gossip by pausing, asking for facts and checking with the person involved rather than believing it or hitting back.
